## Summary

The April 21, 2026 guide describes two custom Payment Element routes. It recommends Checkout Sessions for most integrations, including one-time payments and checkouts with tax, discounts, shipping, or subscriptions. The lower-level Payment Intents route leaves checkout features such as tax, discounts, shipping, and currency conversion to the integration.

The November 7, 2026 capture gives two documentation links. The Checkout Sessions variant uses `payment-ui=embedded-components` and the Payment Intents variant uses `payment-ui=elements`. These query parameters select documentation. The November index supplies no updated integration steps or API and SDK versions.

## April Checkout Sessions route

The April guide uses `ui_mode: "elements"` in its Checkout Sessions example. The Checkout Session client secret initializes Checkout itself. The HTML path uses `stripe.initCheckoutElementsSdk` and confirms with `actions.confirm()` after loading actions. The React path imports from `@stripe/react-stripe-js/checkout`, supplies the secret to `CheckoutElementsProvider`, and uses `checkout.confirm`. Keep this initialization and confirmation separate from Elements initialized with a PaymentIntent or SetupIntent client secret.

The same capture describes Checkout Sessions for both basic payment collection with `price_data` and full line-item checkout, and assigns Adaptive Pricing to Checkout Sessions in this comparison. See the [[source-stripe-checkout-sessions-vs-payment-intents|separate API comparison]].

## April Payment Intents route

The Payment Element supplies payment details to a PaymentIntent for payment or to a SetupIntent to prepare a method for future use. The April guide gives two decisions for this route.

### When to create the Intent

| Approach | Order and use |
| --- | --- |
| **Deferred** | Render the Payment Element first. Create and confirm the PaymentIntent or SetupIntent after the customer submits the payment form. This suits multi-page checkouts and checkouts with changing items, quantities, or discounts. Changing amounts can affect payment method eligibility. Deferring the Intent avoids synchronizing it after every client-side change. |
| **Eager** | Create the PaymentIntent or SetupIntent before loading checkout. Create Elements with that Intent’s `client_secret` so the Payment Element is associated with the Intent. This is the April guide’s quick-start choice for a static checkout. |

### Where to confirm the Intent

| Approach | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| **Client-side** | Client code uses a Stripe SDK to confirm. The SDK handles supported next actions such as 3D Secure and localizes errors. Choose this when the integration does not need server control at confirmation. The integration can still use a backend. |
| **Server-side** | Run the required business logic first, such as applying payment method restrictions or adjusting application fees, then confirm immediately on the server before the client can change the inputs. Handle any returned next actions manually or with a Stripe SDK. The linked PaymentIntent route uses `stripe.handleNextAction` for required customer authentication or redirects. |

Confirmation associates the submitted details with the Intent. Check the resulting state separately for required customer action or a successful payment or setup. The companion [[source-stripe-finalize-payments-server|server-finalization guide]] gives the dated web PaymentIntent `requires_action` example.

payments-payment-element-design-an-integ.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-element/design-an-integration establishes the Payment Element design guide’s purpose and two documentation routes: Checkout Sessions at `payment-ui=embedded-components` and Payment Intents at `payment-ui=elements` (new raw lines 5-14). The April 21 guide recommends Checkout Sessions for most integrations and describes initializing Checkout with the Checkout Session client secret, using `stripe.initCheckoutElementsSdk` and loaded `actions.confirm()` for HTML or `CheckoutElementsProvider` and `checkout.confirm` in React. Its lower-level Payment Intents variant leaves checkout features such as tax and shipping to the integration (old raw lines 8-22). For a multi-page or dynamic checkout, the April guide renders the Payment Element before creating and confirming the relevant Intent on submission, avoiding separate sync as amount and method eligibility change. For a static eager path, create the Intent before loading checkout and pass its client secret into Elements. PaymentIntent collects payment; SetupIntent prepares a future method (old raw lines 28-38). The client SDK handles supported next actions and localization. For server-side business logic, confirm immediately after it runs and handle required next actions manually or through an SDK, such as `stripe.handleNextAction` for the linked PaymentIntent route (old raw lines 40-48). source-stripe-payment-element-design-integration.md captures the two choices but omits the order and required-action qualifications. The revised mapped source preserves the April setup and next-action guidance beside the November selector.
payments-payment-element-design-an-integ.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-element/design-an-integration the November change is variant navigation (new raw lines 9-14 compared with old raw lines 10-18). It does not substantively refresh the April recommendation, lower-level checkout ownership, deferred/eager guidance or client/server handling. Preserve those dated details and their PaymentIntent-versus-SetupIntent purpose (old raw lines 20-48). In source-stripe-payment-element-design-integration.md and its reciprocal Payment Intents concept, clarify that the client confirmation choice concerns control at confirmation and does not mean an integration has no backend. Server confirmation still requires handling any returned next actions, such as customer 3DS or a redirect. Confirming the Intent and associating the submitted payment data do not independently prove payment or setup success. Keep Checkout Sessions-specific client initialization and confirmation separate from the eager Intent client-secret association and the Payment Intent SDK/server paths (old raw lines 8-14, old raw lines 37-38 and old raw lines 40-48). A documentation query parameter is not an API mode, and the selector gives no fresh SDK or API version evidence. The revised source dates the retained design choices and links the companion web server-finalization example.

concept_suggestions.anchor:
| **Deferred** (create Payment Element first) | Multi-page flows; dynamic amounts (items, quantities, discounts can change before Pay) |
| **Eager** (create Intent + Payment Element together) | Static checkout pages; quickest setup |
concept_suggestions.proposed_markdown:
| **Deferred** | Render Payment Element first, then create and confirm the PaymentIntent or SetupIntent on customer submission. Useful for multi-page checkout or changing amounts. |
| **Eager** | Create the PaymentIntent or SetupIntent before loading checkout, then initialize Elements with that Intent’s client secret. The April 2026 guide recommends this for static checkout. |
